main.title: Titanfall
main.subtitle: Agile Pilots and towering Titans fight across the Frontier
main.summary: Titanfall is a 2014 first-person shooter game developed by Respawn Entertainment and published by Electronic Arts. It was released for Windows and Xbox One on March 11, 2014; an Xbox 360 version ported by Bluepoint Games was released April 8, 2014. The game was anticipated as the debut title from developers formerly behind the Call of Duty franchise.

cards.heading: Respawn’s first game brings Pilots and Titans to the Frontier
cards.text: Titanfall is a 2014 first-person shooter game developed by Respawn Entertainment and published by Electronic Arts. It was released for Windows and Xbox One on March 11, 2014; an Xbox 360 version ported by Bluepoint Games was released April 8, 2014. The game was anticipated as the debut title from developers formerly behind the Call of Duty franchise.

cards.heading: Wall-running Pilots and deployable Titans share the battlefield
cards.text: Players fight as agile Pilots across the Frontier's colonies, using wall runs, double jumps and ziplines to link routes through a battlefield. Up to twelve human players take part alongside computer-controlled grunts and spectres. A timer determines when a Pilot can summon a Titan; kills shorten the wait. The machine then drops from the sky, offering heavier armour and weapons in exchange for the Pilot's mobility. Its dash replaces the Pilot's jump. Team objectives bring both scales of combat together, and the losing side finishes with a race to an evacuation dropship. The campaign tells its story through online matches, dialogue and events within them.

cards.heading: Critical reception and the path to Titanfall 2
cards.text: Titanfall won over 60 awards at its E3 2013 reveal, including a record-breaking six E3 Critics Awards and "Best of Show" from several media outlets. It also won awards at Gamescom and the Tokyo Game Show. Titanfall received generally favorable reviews. Reviewers praised its balance, Smart Pistol weapon, player mobility, and overall accessibility for players of all skill sets, but criticized its thin campaign, disappointing artificial intelligence, and lack of community features and multiplayer modes. Critics considered the game a successful evolution for the first-person shooter genre but did not agree as to whether the game delivered on its anticipation. A sequel, Titanfall 2, was released for Windows, PlayStation 4, and Xbox One in 2016.

main.title: Dark Souls II
main.subtitle: An undead traveler searches for a cure in Drangleic
main.summary: Dark Souls II is a 2014 action role-playing game developed by FromSoftware and published by Bandai Namco Games.

cards.heading: A new journey through Drangleic
cards.text: Dark Souls II is FromSoftware's 2014 action role-playing game, published by Bandai Namco. An undead traveller reaches the kingdom of Drangleic searching for a cure to their affliction. Dangerous enemies, limited opportunities to recover health and the risk of losing collected souls shape the journey. Repeated deaths also reduce maximum health through hollowing, giving each attempt a consequence that continues beyond the fight itself.

cards.heading: Death, hollowing and the risk of losing souls
cards.text: Dark Souls II is an entry in the Dark Souls series, known for its difficulty, as both bosses and standard enemies have the potential to defeat the player in only a few hits. As with its predecessor, opportunities for recovering health are limited. With each death, the player's maximum health is reduced. This process, called hollowing, can continue until the HP bar reaches a set lower limit of 50%. The player's full HP bar is only recovered when they expend a rare consumable item. The game uses a form of joint currency called "souls", which are used as both experience points for leveling up and also as currency for purchasing items from shops. Upon death, the player's entire collection of souls is dropped; the player can recover their dropped souls by returning to the spot where they died, but if they die again before picking them up, the souls are permanently lost.

cards.heading: The original 2014 release and its reception
cards.text: After initial delays, Dark Souls II was released worldwide on PlayStation 3 and Xbox 360 in March 2014, with a Windows version released the following month. It was a commercial success and received critical acclaim, with reviewers praising its story, atmosphere, world design and visuals, although they were divided on its difficulty and deemed its boss battles and combat mechanics inferior to the original's. It is the only game in the trilogy to not be directed by series creator Hidetaka Miyazaki.

main.title: Yoshi's New Island
main.subtitle: Protect Baby Mario and open new paths with giant eggs
main.summary: Yoshi's New Island is a 2014 platform game developed by Arzest and published by Nintendo for the Nintendo 3DS. The third installment in the Yoshi's Island series, it is set between the events of Yoshi's Island (1995) and Yoshi's Island DS (2006). The game was released in Europe, North America, and Australia in March 2014 and in Japan in July 2014.

cards.heading: Yoshi carries Baby Mario across a new island
cards.text:
Yoshi's New Island is a 2014 platform game developed by Arzest and published by Nintendo for the Nintendo 3DS. The third installment in the Yoshi's Island series, it is set between the events of Yoshi's Island (1995) and Yoshi's Island DS (2006). The game was released in Europe, North America, and Australia in March 2014 and in Japan in July 2014.

Like its predecessors, Yoshi's New Island's gameplay revolves around safely transporting the infant Mario to his brother Luigi by completing a series of levels across an island. The player characters are dinosaurs known as the Yoshi species; each dinosaur is named Yoshi and has a unique color. In addition to returning mechanics such as hovering, as well as laying and throwing eggs, Yoshis are occasionally able to create massive eggs known as Eggdozers, which can be used to clear paths.

cards.heading: Giant eggs break through obstacles
cards.text: By eating giant Shy Guy enemies or hitting certain blocks, Yoshi can obtain Mega Eggdozers, a feature introduced in Yoshi's New Island. They are massive eggs that can be thrown to destroy normally indestructible terrain and obstacles in the way, providing access to previously obstructed areas as well as potentially earning the player extra lives. A metal variant of the Mega Eggdozer clears paths in addition to weighing Yoshi down, diminishing jumps but allowing for exploration of underwater areas.

cards.heading: A handmade look for the original Nintendo 3DS adventure
cards.text: Nintendo producer Takashi Tezuka had previously directed both Super Mario World (1990) and the original Yoshi's Island. In an interview with Nintendo Life, Tezuka said they chose to develop a sequel to Yoshi's Island over a follow-up to Yoshi's Story (1997), due to the former's simplicity in gameplay and construction, as well as its art style being better suited for the Nintendo 3DS. Oil paintings, watercolors, and crayon drawings in graphics helped retain what Tezuka described as the "warm and friendly vibe" of the original Yoshi's Island, as well as the "handicraft feel" for which the series had become known.

main.title: Luftrausers
main.subtitle: Build an aircraft and survive a sky full of enemies
main.summary: Luftrausers is a shoot 'em up video game developed by Netherlands-based indie developer studio Vlambeer and published by Devolver Digital for Microsoft Windows, OS X, Linux, PlayStation 3 and PlayStation Vita. It was released in March 2014 and ported to Android by General Arcade on May 28, 2015. A demake of the game, titled LuftrauserZ, was developed by Paul Koller for Commodore 64, Commodore 128 and Commodore 64 Games System, and released by RGCD and Vlambeer on December 8, 2017.

cards.heading: Vlambeer expands its aerial combat game
cards.text: Luftrausers is Vlambeer's aerial shoot 'em up, published by Devolver Digital in March 2014 for computers, PlayStation 3 and PlayStation Vita. The aircraft can turn through a full circle, but its gun fires forwards. Surviving therefore depends on controlling its angle and momentum as enemies fill the sky. Different engines, weapons and hulls let the player assemble a machine with its own handling and attacks.

cards.heading: Momentum, aiming and recovery between attacks
cards.text: Thrust, gravity and drift all influence the aircraft's path. Turning its nose towards a target provides an opportunity to shoot, while the plane continues to carry its existing momentum. A circle around the craft shows its remaining health, shrinking as it takes damage. Holding fire allows that health to recover. The player must find moments to stop attacking and stay out of danger before committing to another pass.

cards.heading: Aircraft combinations change the play and the music
cards.text: Aircraft can be customized with dozens of combinations of engines, weapons, and hulls that affect the soundtrack as much as the gameplay. Each weapon part comes with sets of challenges that give objects to strive for, on top of the arcade nature of the game.

main.title: Metal Gear Solid V: Ground Zeroes
main.subtitle: Snake infiltrates Camp Omega in the prologue to The Phantom Pain
main.summary: Metal Gear Solid V: Ground Zeroes is a 2014 action-adventure stealth game developed by Kojima Productions and published by Konami.

cards.heading: Snake infiltrates Camp Omega in 1975
cards.text: Metal Gear Solid V: Ground Zeroes is a 2014 action-adventure stealth game developed by Kojima Productions and published by Konami. It is the eighth main game in the Metal Gear series directed, written, and produced by Hideo Kojima, and serves as a prologue to Metal Gear Solid V: The Phantom Pain, which was released the following year. Set in 1975, a few months after the events of Metal Gear Solid: Peace Walker, the story follows Snake as he infiltrates an American black site in Cuba called Camp Omega, attempting to rescue Cipher agent Paz Ortega Andrade and former Sandinista child soldier Ricardo "Chico" Valenciano Libre.

cards.heading: Reading enemy movements and reacting to detection
cards.text: Snake's binoculars let the player mark guards and follow their positions through the iDroid. Directional, visual and audio cues show when an enemy begins to notice him, providing information for the next move. Being spotted triggers Reflex Mode, a brief window in which Snake can stop the guard before the alarm is raised. Shooting out a light creates another opening for movement. These tools make observing Camp Omega and adjusting a route part of the infiltration.

cards.heading: A stand-alone prologue offers new infiltration routes
cards.text: Camp Omega gives the player room to choose an approach to an objective, using the revised movement and stealth systems to find a route through the base. Ground Zeroes began as part of The Phantom Pain. With the larger game's development taking longer, Kojima Productions released this portion separately, offering an introduction to Metal Gear Solid V's infiltration systems and the events leading into its main campaign.

main.title: inFAMOUS: Second Son
main.subtitle: Delsin explores Seattle with smoke, neon and other powers
main.summary: Infamous Second Son is a 2014 action-adventure video game developed by Sucker Punch Productions and published by Sony Computer Entertainment for the PlayStation 4. The third installment in the Infamous series, it serves as a standalone sequel to 2011's Infamous 2. The player-controlled protagonist possesses superpower abilities that players use in combat and when traveling across the city. The story follows protagonist Delsin Rowe fighting the Department of Unified Protection (D.U.P.) in a fictionalized Seattle. Over the course of the game, Delsin acquires new powers and becomes either good or evil as player choices influence his morality.

cards.heading: Delsin Rowe confronts the D.U.P. in Seattle
cards.text: Infamous Second Son is a 2014 action-adventure video game developed by Sucker Punch Productions and published by Sony Computer Entertainment for the PlayStation 4. The third installment in the Infamous series, it serves as a standalone sequel to 2011's Infamous 2. The player-controlled protagonist possesses superpower abilities that players use in combat and when traveling across the city. The story follows protagonist Delsin Rowe fighting the Department of Unified Protection (D.U.P.) in a fictionalized Seattle. Over the course of the game, Delsin acquires new powers and becomes either good or evil as player choices influence his morality.

cards.heading: Powers change combat and movement through the city
cards.text: Delsin moves through Seattle using powers drawn from smoke, neon, video and concrete. A material can become a weapon or a way through the city: neon, for example, lets him dash up buildings. Using powers drains a meter, which he replenishes from matching sources such as smoke from an exploded vehicle. New power sets introduce abilities through D.U.P. Core Relays, while collected Blast Shards buy further upgrades. Moving, fighting and finding another source of power become connected parts of an encounter.

cards.heading: A new protagonist and a new generation of hardware
cards.text: Sucker Punch began developing Infamous Second Son as early as 2011, when it began discussions with Sony on bringing the Infamous series to a new generation of hardware. The developer provided feedback to Sony on what hardware evolutions it would like to see on PlayStation 4. Sucker Punch considers Second Son a "fresh start" for the series because it features a new protagonist. Delsin's powers were designed to feel fluid and suited to the open world design.

main.title: Diablo III: Reaper of Souls
main.subtitle: A new act, the Crusader and a different path beyond the campaign
main.summary: Reaper of Souls adds a new act and Crusader, then offers a different reason to revisit Diablo III beyond its story.

cards.heading: Westmarch, Malthael and the Crusader
cards.text: Diablo III: Reaper of Souls launched for Windows and Mac on 25 March 2014. Its fifth act takes the fight to Westmarch and Malthael, while the Crusader joins the playable classes. The increased level cap of seventy extends character development alongside the new section of the campaign.

cards.heading: The paid expansion and the preceding free update
cards.text: A free update preceded Reaper of Souls, revising loot, Paragon progression and social features for existing Diablo III players. The expansion added its own campaign act, class and further systems on top of that shared foundation. Players could therefore encounter the revised loot and progression before entering Westmarch or creating a Crusader.

cards.heading: Adventure Mode adds Bounties and Nephalem Rifts
cards.text: Adventure Mode opens the world around Bounties and randomised Nephalem Rifts. Players choose tasks and encounters, then use the rewards to refine their characters and equipment. This gives another session a different structure from progressing through the campaign's story. The Mystic adds further equipment options, allowing a useful item to remain part of that continuing development.

cards.heading: The Mystic changes equipment and appearance
cards.text: The Mystic is a new NPC featured in Diablo III: Reaper of Souls. The mystic serves two basic functions: Item Enchanting and Transmogrification. Item Enchanting allows players to “re-roll the dice”; players are free to re-roll one property on an item. The selected property can be re-rolled to a higher value or to another property. Transmogrification allows players to change their character's appearance for purely aesthetic purposes.

main.title: Age of Wonders III
main.subtitle: Build a fantasy empire and command turn-based battles
main.summary: Age of Wonders III is a 2014 4X turn-based strategy video game developed and published by Dutch developer Triumph Studios. It is the fourth game in the Age of Wonders series, following Age of Wonders, Age of Wonders II: The Wizard's Throne and Age of Wonders: Shadow Magic released in 1999, 2002, and 2003 respectively. It was released on March 31, 2014, through digital distribution, as well as through retail in select territories for Microsoft Windows. A port to Linux and OS X was released on April 14, 2015.

cards.heading: Triumph returns to its fantasy strategy series
cards.text: Age of Wonders III is Triumph Studios' 2014 fantasy strategy game for Windows, the fourth entry in a series begun in 1999. Players explore and expand an empire, deal with other kingdoms and command turn-based battles. A leader's class helps define the options available as the kingdom develops. The campaign sits alongside multiplayer and a level editor; versions for Linux and OS X followed in 2015.

cards.heading: An empire shaped by exploration, diplomacy and leader classes
cards.text: The game is set in a high fantasy fictional setting, where players take the role of a leader to explore the world, interacting with other races and kingdoms, both diplomatically and through warfare while progressively expanding and managing their empire. It features a new graphics engine for the series, in addition to an updated soundtrack. The gameplay has also been updated, featuring a new role-playing style leader class based system and interchangeable choices of strategy and appearances for each playable race. It also supports online and local multiple player modes and a level editor along with a new story driven single player campaign mode.

cards.heading: Tactical battles on a separate hexagonal battlefield
cards.text: When armies meet, the action moves to a separate hexagonal battlefield. Each army holds up to six units, and several armies can join a battle. Players take turns moving their forces and using attacks or abilities. Position matters: walls protect a besieged city, foliage changes the surroundings, and attacking from behind can make a flanking strike more effective. Mana limits the spells available to strengthen troops, summon new units or strike an area. Some spells remain available wherever the leader is, while others require a hero to be present.

main.title: Goat Simulator
main.subtitle: Cause chaos with a goat in an unruly physics playground
main.summary: Goat Simulator turns a badly behaved animal and unreliable physics into a playground for destruction.

cards.heading: An April Fools release turns a goat loose
cards.text: Goat Simulator is Coffee Stain's 2014 physics playground, released on 1 April. Players send a goat through streets and everyday objects, headbutting obstacles, knocking things over and discovering how much destruction they can cause. Erratic movement is part of the comedy, turning a simple action into an unpredictable collision.

cards.heading: Destruction becomes a chain of tricks
cards.text: Scoring draws on skating games, rewarding style and combinations. A headbutt, a backflip and a broken window can become one sequence, with the environment supplying new opportunities to extend it. Players experiment with objects and movement to find an action worth chaining into the next one.

cards.heading: Erratic physics and community creations
cards.text: Coffee Stain deliberately retained amusing physics errors while fixing crashes. Steam Workshop support gave players further ways to expand that approach, with tools for creating goats, levels and missions. The supplied playground became a starting point for community-made variations on its destructive joke.

cards.heading: A game-jam joke becomes a full game
cards.text: Goat Simulator started as a joke prototype from an internal one-month game jam held by Coffee Stain Studios in January 2014, after completing work for their game Sanctum 2. The game was described by Ibrisagic as "an old school skating game, except instead of being a skater, you're a goat, and instead of doing tricks, you wreck stuff". The idea followed after originally pitching the game as a variation of QWOP, where the player would control the individual limbs of the goat separately with various keyboard keys; this concept was rejected in favor of the more Tony Hawk's Pro Skater-type of gameplay the final game presents. Ibrisagic had focused on goats after jokingly trying to convince his coworkers that goats would achieve viral attention on the Internet in much the same way that cats presently do.

main.title: Monument Valley
main.subtitle: Turn impossible monuments into paths for Ida
main.summary: Monument Valley asks the player to guide Ida through architecture that can only work when seen from the right angle.

cards.heading: Guide Ida through impossible architecture
cards.text: Monument Valley is Ustwo's 2014 mobile puzzle game, in which the player guides Ida through impossible architecture. Turning or manipulating a structure can make separated surfaces meet in the view on screen, opening a route for her to walk. The small traveller gives each monument a destination and a scale, while the geometry makes reaching it a puzzle.

cards.heading: Escher, woodblock prints and shifting geometry
cards.text: The team drew on M. C. Escher, Japanese woodblock prints and buildings from around the world. Turning and manipulating the architecture can reveal a connection that ordinary geometry would reject. Ida remains a small, quiet presence inside these carefully composed monuments; the apparent contradiction is something the player can use.

cards.heading: A short journey built around discovery
cards.text: Ustwo designed a short journey with little instruction, restrained sound and animation. Discovering a route carries the experience forward, with the difficulty kept approachable so players can see the remaining monuments. The quiet presentation gives them time to examine a shape, try a transformation and follow the connection it reveals.

cards.heading: A design studio develops a tablet game
cards.text: The tablet game began development in early 2013 under the working title Tower of Illusion. A piece of concept art inspired by M. C. Escher supplied the starting point, and the final design stayed close to it. Ustwo, a digital design studio with experience making mobile apps, gave the team room to concentrate on the result. Development took ten months.

features.title: When an image becomes a path
features.summary: How does Monument Valley turn an optical illusion into a rule the player can use?

cards.heading: A route inside the picture
cards.text: An optical illusion becomes useful when it opens a route for Ida. Turning a monument changes which edges seem to meet, letting the player discover a connection in the image on screen. The composition supplies the information needed to solve the puzzle: the next move begins by looking at how the structure fits together.

cards.heading: Ida gives the structure a scale
cards.text: Ida gives the monument a scale. A ledge becomes somewhere to stand, a staircase becomes a route, and an opening becomes a possible destination. Her small figure helps the player read these relationships while leaving the architecture prominent. Moving her through the scene tests whether the apparent connection can carry the journey forward.

cards.heading: A studio remembers its first release
cards.text: Ustwo's 2024 anniversary account returned to the game's first iOS release on 3 April 2014. A photograph of the team celebrating an App Store feature records the people behind the monuments. The ten-month project had begun with an Escher-inspired drawing, developed by a studio whose wider work included mobile apps and digital design.

cards.heading: An original work, later ways to see it
cards.text: The later Panoramic Edition presents the monuments in a wider frame. Comparing it with the original mobile view draws attention to Ida's position and the amount of architecture visible around her. The framing helps organise a puzzle whose connections must be recognised visually, making the view of a structure part of how it is understood.
